l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Holy Ghost causes Mary to conceive and brings forth the Son of God. It sanctifies high priests and fills people born of God. People are told to receive rather than contend against it; denying it knowingly after it has had place in someone is an unpardonable sin.

l: Lamb of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lamb of God takes away the world’s sins, saving people and cleansing them from all unrighteousness.

l: eternal life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Eternal life is received by beloved brethren who repent and keep God’s commandments, and by people through faith and hope. Those who keep commandments from their covenant receive it according to the Holy Spirit. People are urged to hope and love God, while Lamoni’s father seeks it through repentance and faith.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The kingdom of God is a place of righteous, restored, endless happiness and everlasting praise. Its paths are righteousness, and those who heed God diligently may know its mysteries. It receives the righteous at the last day, when they shine forth after restoration. It excludes filthiness, unclean things, and the wicked. It is inherited by those born again and by a son who repents, forsakes sins and lusts, and is raised to endless happiness.

l: holy order of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The holy order is the order of the Son and has existed from the foundation of the world, without beginning of days or end of years. Priests and high priests are ordained after this order to teach and lead people toward redemption and the rest of the Lord.

l: hope, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_required_with charity The beloved brethren are instructed to have hope along with faith and charity, after which they will always abound in good works.

l: charity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: leads_to good works [with faith and hope] The beloved brethren are instructed to have charity together with faith and hope so that they will always abound in good works.

l: prophets, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: are_holy holy The prophets had spoken prophecies concerning the coming of Christ. Korihor preached against those prophecies, calling them foolish traditions.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Amulek is a Nephite man of Ammonihah, son of Giddonah, a man of reputation, wealth, household, kindreds, and friends. Though called many times, he had hardened his heart until an angel of the Lord confronted him while he traveled to visit kindred. The angel directed him to receive Alma, and Amulek gave Alma food and shelter; Alma blessed his household, kindred, and possessions. Guided by the Spirit, Amulek became a prophet and preacher alongside Alma. In Ammonihah he testified against wickedness, rejected Zeezrom’s offer to deny a Supreme Being, taught one true and living God, the coming Son of God, resurrection, judgment according to works, and redemption for believers. His words silenced Zeezrom. With Alma, he was bound, imprisoned, beaten, mocked, and deprived of necessities. He grieved for women and children cast into flames, then through faith in Christ broke his bonds and survived the prison’s collapse. Rejected by former friends, father, and kindred, he left Ammonihah, forsook possessions for the word of God, and was cared for by Alma in Zarahemla. He continued with Alma and other fellow laborers, preaching repentance and the word in temples, sanctuaries, synagogues, and among the Zoramites. He taught that Christ would atone for the world’s sins and urged faith, repentance, continual prayer, care for those in need, and patience in affliction.

l: Satan, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Satan holds hearts and the people of Ammonihah captive, gaining power to subject people, chain them to destruction, and rule those who harden hearts and die in sins.

l: angel of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: An angel of the Lord delivers a message to Alma, declares repentance to many of God’s people, appears to sorrowful Alma, blesses and reminds him of his first message, then commands him to return to Ammonihah and warn its people to repent or be destroyed.

l: the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Ammonihah reject, revile, and expel Alma, then grow more wicked and seek to destroy liberty. They contend with Alma, question his authority, refuse belief, and seek to imprison him. Hard-hearted, stiffnecked, lost, fallen, and influenced by Satan, they hear Alma and Amulek but many become angry and accuse Amulek. Their sin and transgression bring repeated warnings: repent or face the Lord’s anger and destruction.

l: land of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Korihor went to the land of Gideon and preached against Christ and the prophecies. He had little success there and was taken, bound, and carried before the high priest and chief judge. Gideon is the land to which Pahoran flees after being driven out by the rebels. Pahoran gathers men and receives freemen there.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammonihah is a city and land of the people of Nephi, named for its first possessor. Alma preaches there, is expelled, returns, and later teaches with Amulek; Amulek also warns its people that their sins, rejection of the righteous, and failure to repent could bring famine, pestilence, the sword, and destruction. Its chief judge visits the prison with teachers and lawyers, while people are cast out and Amulek leaves his possessions. The remaining people stay hard-hearted, and the Lamanites invade and destroy Ammonihah, leaving the land desolate for years. Later the city is partly rebuilt, fortified with a high earth ridge and restricted entrance, and successfully defended by the Nephite army against a Lamanite attack.

l: preaching, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Preaching the word of God is conducted in Ammonihah by Alma and Amulek, following the holy order of God through prophecy and revelation. Alma first preaches without being heard, returns by an angel’s command, and with Amulek declares God’s words: repentance, Jesus Christ’s coming, and consequences of righteousness and wickedness.

l: Alma's rejection and expulsion from Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma is rejected and expelled from Ammonihah by its people, who withstand, revile, and spit upon him; he departs sorrowfully until an angel commands his return.

l: the angel's message to Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The angel of the Lord tells Alma to rejoice for his faithfulness, return to Ammonihah, preach again, and warn its people that destruction will come unless they repent.

l: Amulek's feeding Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: After Alma returns to Ammonihah, Amulek recognizes him as a holy prophet, takes him home, feeds him after fasting, and receives Alma’s blessing and thanks to God.

l: Alma and Amulek's preaching, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma and Amulek preach and prophesy among the people of Ammonihah. Filled with the Holy Ghost, they receive power from the Lord against confinement and death, continuing until they are bound and cast into prison.

l: liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Liberty is a God-granted freedom, protected by statutes, judgments, and commandments and preserved by the Nephites as a remnant of Joseph. It is bound to rights, religion, and a free government maintained by freemen. The Nephites fight and cry to the Lord to preserve it from bondage, while Moroni labors for it, rejoices in it, and acts against threats that could overthrow it. Freemen covenant to maintain it and suppress the king-men’s attempt to overturn their government. Pahoran urges resistance to evil to retain the liberty God made them free in. Finally, Moroni raises the standard of liberty, gathering thousands to defend their freedom.

l: destruction of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_conditioned_on repentance [the people must repent to avoid it] The angel of the Lord tells Alma to warn the people of Ammonihah that the Lord God will destroy them unless they repent. The text records the warning, not the destruction itself.

l: imprisonment of Alma and Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma and Amulek are bound and imprisoned for many days, questioned, beaten, mocked, and deprived, until they break their strong cords through God's power.

l: Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lehi is a Nephite military leader, one of Zoram’s two sons, who came from the land of Jerusalem and was a father in Alma’s line. He helps recover captives, then repeatedly serves with Moroni in major battles. He conceals an army near hill Riplah, attacks the Lamanites from behind, and drives them across the river Sidon. Moroni appoints him chief captain over the city of Noah, where the Lamanites fear him greatly. He protects Bountiful with a small army, takes command of Mulek, and later shares command of Moroni’s army and the war with Teancum. He rejoices with Moroni and mourns Teancum’s death.

l: people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Ammonihah are a hard-hearted, stiffnecked group who forget their fathers’ traditions and the commandments of God, become angry at Alma’s description, reject repentance, and attribute Alma and Amulek’s power to Satan. They belong to the profession of Nehor and are ultimately destroyed by the Lamanites, with every living soul killed.

l: the land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The land is promised to prosper those who keep God’s commandments. Those who refuse to keep them may be cut off from the presence of the Lord and destroyed from the face of the earth.

l: the wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_filled_with wild animals [of every kind] A narrow strip of wilderness divides the land of Zarahemla from the Lamanites and Nephites. The wilderness contains Lamanite settlements and borders the lands on the north and south.

l: the presence of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The presence of the Lord is what mankind was cut off from through spiritual death. The resurrection of the dead brings men back into the presence of God to be judged.

l: destruction of the people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The destruction of Ammonihah is first prophesied as a possible one-day calamity if its people persist in wickedness. Their lawyers’ and judges’ unrighteousness lays its foundation, though repentance could avert it. Despite disbelief, the Lamanites enter from Zarahemla’s borders, fall upon Ammonihah, and destroy its people.

l: judgment day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Judgment day is the last day when all people stand before the Son of God and are judged by their works; it will be more tolerable for the Lamanites than sinful Ammonihah.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The coming of Christ is presented as a long-expected, near event: the kingdom of heaven is nigh, priests preach it, and the Son of God is expected to come in glory. Angels will declare the coming to just and holy men, fulfilling the fathers’ words, while Alma awaits it with joy. It is taught that the Son of God will shortly come and later appear after his resurrection. Converted Lamanites look forward to it, though the Zoramites deny any Christ. The coming centers on taking away the sins of the world, declaring salvation, and preparing people and their children to hear the word.

l: war against the people of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lamanites make preparations for war against the people of God and come to destroy the king and the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi offer no resistance.

l: damnation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_reaped_by the evil [according to the power and captivation of the devil] Damnation of the soul is the result awaiting those who are evil, according to the power and captivation of the devil.

l: prison, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The prison confines Alma and Amulek for many days as they are bound, mocked, beaten, and deprived; after they break their cords, its walls are rent in twain and collapse to the earth.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Zeezrom is a man and expert lawyer with much business among the people, initially foremost in accusing Amulek and Alma. Expert in devices of the devil, he tries to induce Amulek to deny a Supreme Being and uses subtle plans and lies to deceive people. Amulek’s words make him tremble, and Alma exposes his lies to God and men. Zeezrom becomes conscious of his guilt, convinced of God’s power, and diligently asks about the kingdom of God and resurrection. He recognizes Alma and Amulek as spotless, pleads for them, and is cast out by the people. In Sidom, tribulation and sin leave him sick with a burning fever; believing Alma’s words about Christ’s redemption, he is healed through faith, baptized unto the Lord, and preaches in Sidom. He later goes with Alma among the Zoramites as a fellow laborer, to preach the word.

l: angel of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: gave angel's commission to Amulek The angel of the Lord appears to Amulek while he is journeying and commands him to return home, receive Alma, and feed him. The angel says Alma is a holy and chosen man of God and promises blessings upon Amulek and his house.

l: lawyers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lawyers are a profession hired or appointed to administer law before judges, learned in arts and cunning. Seeking gain, they chiefly work through Zeezrom to accuse and trap Amulek and Alma and pervert righteous ways.

l: kingdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The kingdom is sought through bondage, then obtained by Amalickiah through assassination, fraud, cunning servants, and marriage to the queen.

l: law, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The law is called just by the people of Ammonihah, though they accuse Alma and Amulek of reviling it. Amulek defends the law while condemning the people’s unrighteousness. It affixes punishment, reveals sin, and, through justice, brings remorse unless mercy claims the creature. Later, people seek changes to it, but Pahoran refuses to alter it.

l: prayers of the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: spare people of Ammonihah [from utter destruction] The prayers of the righteous are the reason the people have been spared from utter destruction. Amulek says that without those prayers, destruction would come by famine, pestilence, and the sword.

l: angel's commission to Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: An angel instructs Amulek to return home, receive and feed Alma, promising blessings for his household; Amulek obeys and finds Alma.

l: Amulek's testimony, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: testifies_of things of God [true according to Amulek] Amulek testifies that Alma is a holy man and that Alma’s teachings are true because an angel of God made these things manifest to him. He also testifies that Alma’s presence brought blessings to his household and kindred.

l: questioning of Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_conducted_by lawyers [to make him cross or contradict his words] The lawyers begin questioning Amulek in order to make him contradict himself and create evidence against him. Amulek perceives their designs and condemns their attempts to trap the holy ones of God.

l: Shiblon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Shiblon, Alma’s son, is praised for faithfulness, diligence, patience, and long-suffering among the Zoramites despite bonds and stoning for the word’s sake. From youth he looked to the Lord Jesus Christ, walked uprightly before God, kept commandments, and taught the people. He received the sacred things from Helaman, later conferred them upon Helaman’s son before his death, and died in the thirty-ninth year.

l: Supreme Being, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_exists true and living God The existence of a Supreme Being was challenged by Zeezrom, but Amulek affirmed it.

l: temporal death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Temporal death is a death of mortality that separates soul and body and precedes resurrection. It came through being cut off from the tree of life and the face of the earth, and is not reclaimed by the plan of redemption because doing so would destroy the plan of happiness. After death, the spirit awaits resurrection in happiness or misery; all people are raised as spirit and body reunite in a perfect, immortal form. Mortal deaths also spread through murder and war, worsened by insufficient government strength and succor.

l: death of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: looses temporal death [its bands] The death of Christ will loose the bands of temporal death so that all people will be raised from temporal death.

l: body, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The body remains separate from the soul between death and resurrection, then reunites with it in restoration. Every part, including hair, limbs, and joints, is restored to a proper, perfect frame, and mortality is raised to immortality.

l: Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Spirit is poured out on the land to prepare people, commands a son through the speaker, and overpowers Lamoni, the queen, Ammon, and servants so they fall to earth.

l: Adam, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Adam is a fallen man who fell by partaking of forbidden fruit, bringing temporal death and making mankind lost and fallen. After gaining knowledge of good and evil, he was cut off from the tree of life; otherwise he would have lived forever without space for repentance.

l: our first parents, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Our first parents, after the Fall, were sent from the garden of Eden and cut off from the tree of life and the Lord’s presence, temporally and spiritually. They became subject to their own will; they could not partake of the tree lest they remain forever miserable without a preparatory state, requiring redemption, death, and judgment.

l: angels, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Angels declare the Lord’s voice and glad tidings to all nations and peoples, preparing children of men to receive the word at the Son’s coming, when they will speak to just and holy men.

l: second death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Second death is spiritual death concerning righteousness, following temporal death in sins and culminating in everlasting destruction.

l: immortality, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: follows temporal death [through resurrection] After being raised from mortality, people are brought to an immortal state in which the soul can never die. Immortality is discussed in connection with the resurrection and judgment.

l: the probationary state, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The probationary state is this life after death came upon mankind. It is a preparatory time for people to repent, serve God, perform their labors, meet conditions for mercy, and prepare to meet God and for eternity after the resurrection. It ends when the night of darkness comes, when no labor can be performed.

l: righteousness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Righteousness is subject to spiritual death; unrepentant people face everlasting death and destruction, while those who repent, desire it to life’s end, and act righteously are rewarded and restored unto it.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Mercy comes through the Only Begotten Son and is available to those who repent and do not harden their hearts. It brings remission of sins, God’s rest, faith unto repentance, safety, and rescue from death and misery. God shows mercy by making the plan of salvation known, sending angels, hearing prayers and cries, and turning judgments away because of his Son. It extends over all the earth, yet claims only the truly penitent through the atonement. Mercy satisfies and overpowers justice without robbing or destroying it, while it is restored to those who are merciful to their brethren.

l: justice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Justice is the just, demanding force of the whole law: it judges hearts, words, works, and thoughts; requires restoration to proper order; and requires punishment, including the life of a murderer. It exposes those without faith to the law’s demands and consigns unrepentant mankind forever to be cut off from God’s presence. Mercy may satisfy its demands only through faith unto repentance; the plan of redemption cannot destroy or rob justice.

l: holy scriptures, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Holy scriptures are records containing the fall of man and teaching worship, prayer, the Son of God, mercy, commandments, transgression, and redemption. Some seek and expound them diligently, beginning with Adam’s creation; they testify through prophets of old. The people finally cast these records into fire to destroy them.

l: garden of Eden, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The garden of Eden is a garden containing the tree of life; after the fall, the Lord God sent the first parents forth to till the ground and guarded its east with cherubim and a flaming sword.

l: lake of fire and brimstone, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a torment [for those chained down to everlasting destruction] The torments of those who die spiritually are described as being like a lake of fire and brimstone whose flame ascends forever and ever.

l: everlasting destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_caused_by Satan [through his power and captivity] Everlasting destruction is the fate of those chained down by Satan's power and captivity or condemned through unrepented iniquity. It is connected with spiritual death and the inability of justice to be destroyed.

l: Melchizedek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Melchizedek is a high priest after the holy order of God and king of Salem. He receives that priesthood, preaches repentance to his wicked people, and after they repent establishes peace in the land, becoming called the prince of peace.

l: high priests, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: High priests are priests of God called by faith and ordained in the holy order to teach commandments so people may enter the Lord’s rest. Through faith, repentance, and righteousness they are sanctified by the Holy Ghost, their garments washed white through the Lamb’s blood, and they reject sin with abhorrence.

l: the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people are taught by priests to look forward to the Son, repent righteously, humble themselves, cast off sins, bring forth repentance’s fruit, receive remission, and enter the Lord’s rest.

l: fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The fathers were in bondage and afflicted by hunger and thirst; God alone delivered them, bringing them from Egypt and Jerusalem, while their genealogy was preserved on brass plates.

l: land of Salem, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The land of Salem was ruled by Melchizedek when its people had become full of wickedness and abomination. Peace was established in the land after the people repented.

l: holy calling, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The holy calling, prepared from the world's foundation for faithful doers of good, leads those who receive it to ordination in the high priesthood of the holy order.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Atonement of Christ is the infinite and eternal sacrifice of the Only Begotten Son, made through the Son of God’s suffering, death, and shed blood for the sins and iniquities of the world. It is required for redemption because without it all mankind would unavoidably perish; only an infinite atonement can suffice. Through faith and repentance, it atones for sins and offers mercy. It also brings about the plan of mercy, appeases the demands of justice, breaks the bands of death, swallows up death’s sting in hopes of glory, and brings to pass the resurrection of the dead. Prepared from the foundation of the world, it is taught as the means of redemption, though Korihor denied that any atonement could be made. Alma’s remembrance that Jesus Christ would come to atone led him to cry for mercy.

l: rest of the Lord their God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_entered_by the people [through repentance and purity] The high priesthood is taught so that people may enter into the rest of the Lord. Those who are made pure and spotless before God enter into that rest.

l: ordinances, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The ordinances of the holy order are a type of the Son of God's order, helping people look forward to the Only Begotten Son for remission of sins and entry into the Lord's rest.

l: glad tidings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Glad tidings are declarations of great joy to all nations about Christ’s coming and salvation. Angels and the Son declare them, preparing scattered people’s minds and hearts to receive the word and Christ.

l: day of salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: draws_nigh repentance [as the time to repent] Alma declares that the day of salvation is drawing near and calls on the people to repent.

l: people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A group largely opposes Alma and Amulek after their teachings. They testify before the chief judge, expel and burn believers and records, abuse the two men, then flee in fear when the prison collapses.

l: wives and children of the expelled believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Wives and children of expelled believers are gathered and burned in fire; though Amulek grieves, Alma does not intervene, saying the Spirit restrains him; they are received by the Lord.

l: fire, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: consumes holy scriptures [when the records are cast into it] The fire consumes the women, children, and other believers who are cast into it, as well as the records containing the holy scriptures.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Faith of Christ grants Alma and Amulek power to break bonds and survive a prison’s collapse. Held firmly by the people of Ammon, it gives hope concerning death and resurrection; those who die in it are happy and redeemed by the Lord Jesus Christ. Moroni also holds it firmly while defending his people, rights, country, and religion.

l: miraculous power of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The miraculous power of God delivers and preserves people, causes servants to fall, and enables mighty miracles. It comes upon Alma and Amulek, allowing them to rise, break strong cords, and leave a fallen prison unharmed. It is recognized in the falling of the king, queen, servants, and Ammon, strengthens Ammon and his brethren in their work and escape from imprisonment, brings many Lamanites to repentance, and preserves the wounded two thousand and sixty through faith and God's goodness.

l: martyrdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: consumes women and children [by fire] Alma and Amulek are carried to the place of martyrdom to witness the destruction of those consumed by fire.

l: martyrdom of the believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The martyrdom of those who believed includes believers, women, and children being burned, while Alma and Amulek witness it. Alma says the Lord permits it because of hardened hearts. Later, rulers have believers in the Lord and his power put to death, stirring anger among their brethren and causing contention in the wilderness.

l: collapse of the prison, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: slays people [except Alma and Amulek] The earth shakes mightily and the prison walls are rent in twain and fall to the earth. The chief judge, lawyers, priests, teachers, and every soul within the walls except Alma and Amulek are slain, while Alma and Amulek come forth unharmed.

l: land of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: contains people who had departed out of the land of Ammonihah [expelled believers] The land of Sidom was where Alma and Amulek found people who had departed from Ammonihah. Zeezrom was healed there, Alma established a church there, and many people from the surrounding region were baptized.

l: people who had departed out of the land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: People who believed Alma were cast out of Ammonihah and stoned, then told Alma and Amulek what happened to them and their families.

l: people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Sidom were astonished by Zeezrom’s healing; as knowledge spread, many were baptized, humbled themselves before God, worshipped at sanctuaries, and continually prayed for deliverance.

l: power of Christ unto salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: can_heal Zeezrom [if believed in] Alma asked Zeezrom whether he believed in the power of Christ unto salvation. Zeezrom affirmed his belief.

l: redemption of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Redemption of Christ is the reclaiming of mankind from spiritual death, accomplished through the death, sufferings, and blood atonement of the Son of God. It is part of God’s plan of mercy and eternal purposes. The Son of God comes to redeem his people; belief in this redemption can bring healing.

l: healing of Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: was_done_by Lord [according to Zeezrom's faith in Christ] The healing of Zeezrom occurred after Alma prayed to the Lord for mercy and asked that Zeezrom be healed according to his faith in Christ. Zeezrom leaped to his feet and walked, astonishing the people.

l: baptism of Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma baptized Zeezrom unto the Lord after Zeezrom was healed. Zeezrom began preaching to the people from that time forth.

l: church in the land of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: had_leaders priests and teachers in the land of Sidom [consecrated by Alma] Alma established a church in the land of Sidom and consecrated priests and teachers to baptize those who desired baptism.

l: baptism of the people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Many people from the region around Sidom were baptized after the church was established there.

l: humbling of the people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people in Sidom began to humble themselves before God after a great check as to the pride of their hearts. They assembled at their sanctuaries to worship God and watched and prayed continually.

l: Ammonihahites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A people of Nehor’s profession, the Ammonihahites are destroyed; their great city becomes desolate in one day.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The armies of the Lamanites are Lamanite forces, including several descended or dissenting groups, armed with swords, cimeters, bows, arrows, stones, and slings but generally lacking defensive armor. They enter through the wilderness, destroy Ammonihah, take captives, and are scattered by Nephite armies. Though more than twice as numerous as the Nephites, they suffer losses and flee toward the river Sidon. Divided between the king’s loyal forces and Lehonti’s forces, they come under Amalickiah’s leadership. They fail against fortified cities at Ammonihah and Noah, then later gain Nephite cities on the west sea while Moroni is absent.

l: Nephite armies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Nephite armies, led by Zoram, fortify and grow for protection, then cross Sidon into the south wilderness, defeat Lamanites and recover captives; later they expand defenses, secure borders, and defeat Morianton's army.

l: captives, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Captives are taken by Lamanites into the wilderness, then recovered without loss of life by Nephites.

l: Zoram, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Zoram, brought from Jerusalem, became Nephite chief captain; with sons Lehi and Aha, he sought Alma’s guidance and led recovery of captives.

l: Aha, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Aha was one of Zoram's two sons and helped lead the Nephite armies in searching for and recovering the captives.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Moroni is a Nephite chief captain and military commander, appointed over the armies at age twenty-five. He leads the Nephites through wars against the Lamanites and internal dissenters, combining stratagem, intelligence, fortified defenses, and continual preparation. Although strong, mighty, and effective in battle, he does not delight in bloodshed or murder; his central commitments are the liberty, safety, religion, and welfare of his people, faith in Christ, fear of God, and obedience to covenants. He raises and plants the title of liberty, leads action against Amalickiah and the king-men, and seeks peace by requiring enemies to surrender weapons and covenant not to return to war. He builds forts, earthworks, walls, strongholds, guarded borders, and fortified cities, appoints leaders including Lehi and Teancum, drives back Lamanite forces, and captures places such as Mulek, Gid, and Nephihah. Wounded in battle and burdened by losses, he still protects prisoners, women, and children, and seeks to preserve his people rather than destroy enemies. After receiving reports from Helaman and disputing with Pahoran over neglected armies, he joins Pahoran under the standard of liberty, restores peace in Zarahemla, defeats remaining enemies, fortifies the land, gives command to his son Moronihah, and dies at the end of the thirty-sixth year of the reign of the judges.

l: Manti, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a land [target of the Lamanite advance] Manti is the land the Lamanites intend to possess and attack through its weaker part. Moroni marches there, gathers its people for battle, and arranges the Nephite ambush nearby.

l: Desolation of Nehors, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Land formerly called Ammonihah, renamed for slain followers of Nehor after its destruction, and left desolate thereafter.

l: synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Synagogues are built after Nehors’ order by Amalekites and Amulonites, in Ishmael by Lamoni, where Aaron preaches.

l: sons of Mosiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The sons of Mosiah are a group who once went with Alma seeking to destroy the church of God until a holy angel stopped them. They gained strong knowledge and understanding through scripture study, prayer, and fasting, receiving prophecy and revelation. Refusing the kingdom Mosiah wished to confer, they left Zarahemla and taught the word of God among the Lamanites for fourteen years despite afflictions.

l: Aaron and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Aaron and his brethren go to the land of Nephi and appear before the king who was Lamoni’s father. They teach the king and later preach to the multitude after the king commands them to do so.

l: land of Ishmael, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The land of Ishmael, named after Ishmael, is the inheritance of Ammon and Lamoni. Ammon is bound and brought before Lamoni there, then serves and watches flocks. Later Lamoni builds synagogues and teaches there; Ammon teaches its people, outside Lamoni’s father’s rule.

l: the waters of Sebus, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The waters of Sebus are a place of water where Lamanitish servants bring king Lamoni’s flocks to drink. Lamanites scatter the flocks, Ammon defends them, and later a man attacking Ammon over his slain brother falls dead there.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lamoni is a king over the land and people of Ishmael, a descendant of Ishmael, son of another king, husband and father, and owner of the king’s flocks. He first employs Ammon to watch his flocks, then is pleased with him, frees him from bands, and offers him a daughter in marriage. After learning of Ammon’s faithfulness and power, Lamoni believes Ammon is the Great Spirit, accepts his teaching about God and redemption, prays for mercy, and collapses as if dead. After two days and nights he awakens, says he has seen his Redeemer, and is filled with joy. He teaches his people the words he heard from Ammon. Later he travels with Ammon toward Middoni, refuses his father’s command to slay Ammon, helps free Aaron and his brethren, retains his kingdom, builds synagogues, and grants his people liberty to worship the Lord.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon is a Nephite man, son of Mosiah and brother of Aaron, Omner, Himni, and Alma. Called by the Holy Spirit, he becomes a missionary and preacher among the Lamanites, receiving knowledge and power through faith and desire in God. He journeys to Ishmael, chooses to serve king Lamoni, and proves his great strength while defending the king’s flocks: he gathers scattered flocks, kills attackers, and cuts off the arms of others. Through the Spirit of God he discerns Lamoni’s thoughts, teaches Lamoni, the queen, servants, and the people about God, the scriptures, redemption, and Christ, and continues teaching them righteousness and the commandments. He knows Lamoni is not dead, prays and gives thanks, and is overcome with joy. Directed by the Lord, he goes to Middoni to free his imprisoned brethren, protects Lamoni from his father, defeats an attack, and helps secure both his brethren’s release and Lamoni’s rule. Protected so he can preach freely, he later counsels with Lamoni and Anti-Nephi-Lehi as the Lamanites prepare against them. With compassion for the people, he asks that they flee to the Nephites, seeks the Lord’s direction, leads them toward Zarahemla, meets Alma, and helps bring them to Jershon. Ammon sees himself as weak personally but as an instrument in God’s hands. His central joy is God’s power, the repentance of many thousands, the success and safety of his brethren, and the Lord’s mercy and answers to prayer.

l: Lamanitish servants, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lamanitish servants serve king Lamoni as flock watchers. With Ammon, they drive the flocks to Sebus, fear death when they scatter, and follow his instructions to recover them. They prepare horses for the king’s journey and testify to Lamoni of Ammon’s defense, preservation of their lives, strength, and the power of God. After falling to the earth when the Lord is called upon, their hearts change and they no longer desire evil.

l: the king’s flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: King Lamoni’s flocks are driven to and watered at the waters of Sebus, where brethren scatter them. Ammon and the servants gather, protect, water, and return them to the king’s pasture, preventing further scattering while he is present.

l: slings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon uses his sling with mighty power to cast stones at the Lamanites who scatter the flocks. He kills six of them with the sling.

l: arms, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_smitten_off_by Ammon [with the edge of his sword] Ammon smites off the arms of the men who lift clubs against him. The severed arms are carried before king Lamoni as testimony of what the attackers did.

l: truth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The sons of Mosiah grow strong in the knowledge of the truth and bring many Lamanites to that knowledge through their teaching. The Lamanites who are brought to believe and know the truth become firm and are willing to suffer unto death rather than commit sin. More than a thousand are brought to a knowledge of the truth.

l: prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Prayer is continual turning and calling to God, heard sincerely in affliction and remembered as heard by the Lord. It should acknowledge unworthiness and seek mercy, strength, comfort, wisdom, and success. It may be offered privately, among a congregation, and in wilderness, fields, houses, or closets, including over enemies, crops, and flocks. The Zoramites’ repeated prayer of separation contrasts with faithful prayer, which keeps the heart drawn out to God and requires charitable action.

l: afflictions, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Afflictions are sufferings such as travel, privation, rejection, mocking, beatings, imprisonment, trials, and troubles. Ammon and his brethren endure them while preaching to save souls. People are exhorted to bear all afflictions patiently, with firm hope and without reviling others; through trust in God, they can be overcome and bring deliverance and lifting up at the last day.

l: journey from Zarahemla to Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: In the first year of the judges, the sons of Mosiah and selected companions leave Zarahemla with supplies for the wilderness, bound for Nephi to preach to the Lamanites and save souls. They separate at the Lamanite borders, endure privation and affliction, rely on God’s mercies, and hope to reunite after their harvest.

l: teaching among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: For fourteen years, Ammon's brethren teach the word of God among the Lamanites. Despite being cast out, mocked, beaten, stoned, bound, and imprisoned while teaching widely, they endure with patience and are delivered by God. Their work succeeds in bringing many Lamanites to knowledge of the truth.

l: conversion of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The conversion of the Lamanites is a work God brings about through the power of his word, fulfilling his purpose to restore many thousands to truth. The sons of Mosiah begin by seeking their repentance and knowledge of redemption. After losses and afflictions, many remember Aaron and his brethren’s preaching, reject inherited traditions, believe in the Lord, and are converted. Thousands leave darkness for God’s light and salvation, showing change through love and rejecting violence and sin. God’s power in them will continue in future generations.

l: Ammon becoming Lamoni's servant, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon becomes king Lamoni’s servant, declines marriage to a daughter, and is assigned with other servants to watch Lamoni’s flocks.

l: the scattering of the flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Certain Lamanites scatter Lamoni’s flocks at Sebus, causing Ammon and the other servants to fear king Lamoni will kill them.

l: Ammon's defense of the flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon defends Lamoni’s flocks by directing servants, driving away attackers with sling stones, killing some, cutting off club-wielders’ arms with a sword, and restoring the flocks to the king.

l: records, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The records are sacred plates of Nephi containing holy scriptures and the people’s history, including Laman and Lemuel’s rebellions. Helaman receives and must preserve them for a wise purpose: to enlarge memory, reveal God’s power, convince people to repent, and bring them to salvation. They remain protected if he keeps God’s commandments.

l: the fall of man, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The fall of man results from transgression, bringing temporal and spiritual death to all mankind, making humanity carnal, sensual, and devilish, and creating the need for redemption.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The plan of redemption is prepared from the foundation of the world through Christ. It includes the coming of Christ and is taught by Ammon and Aaron to king Lamoni, his servants, and all who believe on Christ’s name. God makes the plan of salvation known through mercy and angels, and it is to be declared to every soul, including the Zoramites and their children, so they may repent and come unto God. It depends on a space for repentance; it would have been frustrated if Adam had partaken of the tree of life and lived forever before repentance.

l: the king who was Lamoni’s father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lamoni’s father is a king over nearly all the land of Nephi and Lamoni’s father. At first, angered by Lamoni’s intent to help Ammon’s brethren, he orders violence against Ammon and attacks him, but yields after Ammon overcomes him, releasing the brethren and preserving Lamoni’s kingdom. He later receives Aaron and his brethren, seeks understanding of the Spirit, repentance, and Ammon’s words, believes, prays, and desires eternal life. After being raised by Aaron, he is converted with his household, ministers and pacifies his people, authorizes preaching, issues protective proclamations, and consults on a name for the converted people.

l: queen (wife of king Lamoni), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Queen, wife of king Lamoni, believes Ammon, is blessed for exceeding faith and saved by Jesus, falls under the Spirit’s power, then rises when Abish takes her hand.

l: Abish, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Abish is a Lamanitish woman converted to the Lord for many years after her father’s remarkable vision. Knowing God’s power, she remains standing, gathers people at the king’s house, and raises the queen and king.

l: the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: People gather at the king’s house and contend over Ammon; many hear teachings, believe the king’s words, are converted to the Lord, and are baptized.

l: Great Spirit, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Great Spirit is believed by some to be Ammon or to have sent him, attending Nephites and afflicting people for iniquities after destruction of Lamanites.

l: the sword, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The sword causes the deaths of thousands and is used by the Lamanites against the people. Moroni says he will take up the sword against the government if necessary to defend freedom and obtain food.

l: conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Conversion is a turning to the Lord, brought about by preaching the word and, in Abish’s case, her father’s remarkable vision. Abish has long been converted; missionaries, Lamoni, Ammon, and servants lead many others, including the king’s household, to truth. Those converted reject war, bury their weapons, and rely on God.

l: king Lamoni's awakening, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: occurs_after two days and two nights Lamoni awakens on the morrow according to Ammon's words. He rises, praises God, declares that he has seen his Redeemer, and later teaches his people.

l: the servants' falling to the earth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_caused_by fear of the Lord The servants call on the name of the Lord in their might and all fall to the earth except Abish. They later testify that their hearts were changed and that they no longer desired to do evil.

l: the sword attack on Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: fails_against Ammon [the attacker falls dead] A man whose brother was slain by Ammon raises a sword to kill Ammon. Before striking him, the man falls dead, and the people fear and marvel.

l: the gathering at the king's house, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: includes the people [a multitude] Abish runs from house to house and makes the events known, causing a multitude to gather at the king's house. The people see the king, queen, servants, and Ammon lying on the earth.

l: establishment of the church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: occurs_among Lamanites [after their conversion] The people who believe and are baptized become a righteous people and establish a church among themselves.

l: the work of the Lord among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: commences_among Lamanites The work of the Lord commences among the Lamanites as the Lord begins to pour out his Spirit upon them. The account says that his arm is extended to all people who repent and believe on his name.

l: iniquity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Iniquity is a hated source of mourning, hardened hearts, secret combinations, suffering, and destruction among the people of God. It grows from sin and wickedness, including leaders seeking power, and is foretold to become great among the people of Nephi by the fourth generation, fulfilling destruction. Rebels cause great iniquity by taking Zarahemla and allying with the Lamanites; Pahoran seeks to end it by reclaiming the city, and Moroni ends it through action against dissenters.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Aaron, Ammon’s brother and Alma’s fellow laborer, is a preacher of the word of God. He is led to the land of Nephi, preaches repentance, Christ, resurrection, redemption, and atonement, and is repeatedly rejected and imprisoned before being delivered. He travels with his brethren to the king who was Lamoni’s father, expounds the scriptures and the plan of redemption, administers to the king, and raises him after he falls as if dead. Protected by the king of the Lamanites, Aaron goes from city to city preaching, establishes churches, and consecrates priests and teachers. Many Lamanites later remember his and his brethren’s words, believe, and are converted. He later accompanies Alma among the Zoramites, where Alma prays for his comfort and strength in Christ.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon’s brethren are a group of just, holy prophets and Ammon’s brothers who preach among the Lamanites. They separate in the borders of the land of the Lamanites and journey in the land of Nephi, laboring exceedingly despite rejection, beating, imprisonment, hunger, thirst, nakedness, binding, violence, and other afflictions. They endure patiently and are released from imprisonment in Middoni through Lamoni and Ammon. Saved by God from their sinful state, they become instruments of God in bringing Lamanites to repentance. Their preaching, records, and words convince many thousands, bring much fruit, and produce success, joy, reception, and safety in the land of Jershon.

l: land of Middoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Middoni is a land ruled by Antiomno where Aaron, Ammon’s brethren, and other brethren preach, are imprisoned, and are ultimately brought out when Lamoni and Ammon arrive and its king favors Lamoni.

l: Lamoni's kingdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_retained_by Lamoni [from this time and forever] Lamoni’s kingdom is preserved when Ammon requires Lamoni’s father to allow Lamoni to retain it. Lamoni’s father grants that Lamoni may retain the kingdom from that time and forever and will govern him no more.

l: journey to Middoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon and Lamoni travel by horses and chariots toward Middoni, meet Lamoni’s father, then continue to Middoni.

l: imprisonment of Ammon's brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: has_condition strong cords Ammon’s brethren are taken and cast into prison in the land of Middoni, where they are bound with strong cords and kept for many days. Their imprisonment follows their rejection, beatings, and forced movement from house to house and place to place.

l: deliverance of Ammon's brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: After suffering in prison in Middoni, Ammon and Lamoni seek and obtain the release of Aaron and his brethren, who are brought forth and go again to declare the word.

l: soul, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The soul exists in happiness or misery between death and resurrection, then is restored to its body through Christ’s power and brought before God for judgment.

l: Amalekites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Amalekites are a hardened Lamanite people, many following Nehors, who build Jerusalem, synagogues, and sanctuaries. An Amalekite rejects and mocks Aaron’s teachings about Christ. They repeatedly stir unconverted Lamanites and Amulonites to anger, form the greatest number who slay Anti-Nephi-Lehi’s people, and never join the people of the Lord. Angry over losses, they renew destruction and later serve as chief captains under Zerahemnah, inspiring battle.

l: Amulonites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Lamanite group that stirs anger against Anti-Nephi-Lehi, slays brethren most, and never joins the people of the Lord.

l: the people of Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Lamoni, under Lamoni’s reign in Ishmael, become free from his father’s oppressions, receive liberty to worship God, and are continually taught by Ammon. They heed the word daily, keep God’s commandments zealously, and are also taught by Lamoni.

l: death and sufferings of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Aaron teaches that the death and sufferings of Christ are required for the redemption of mankind.

l: imprisonment of Aaron and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: involves suffering [many things] Aaron and a certain number of his brethren are taken and cast into prison in Middoni. They suffer many things before being delivered.

l: the queen, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a queen [of the king who was Lamoni’s father] The queen is told that the king has fallen as if dead and commands the servants to slay Aaron and his brethren. When the servants fear, she also fears and commands that the people be called to slay them.

l: Omner, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Omner, Alma’s fellow laborer and a preacher, goes among the Zoramites; Alma prays he will be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: the servants of the king, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: fear Aaron and his brethren [because of their perceived power] The servants see the cause of the king’s fall and refuse to lay their hands on Aaron and his brethren because they fear them. They tell the queen that one of Aaron’s group is mightier than they are and later report the king’s condition to her.

l: the king’s household, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The king ministers to his whole household, and all are converted unto the Lord.

l: Bountiful, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Bountiful is the land southward of the line dividing it from Desolation, spanning the east sea to the west sea. Nephites inhabit its wilderness of wild animals; on its border with Desolation, Hagoth builds an exceedingly large ship.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Desolation is the land northward of Bountiful, bordering it from east sea to west sea, near Hagoth’s shipbuilding place; it reaches a far northern land once peopled, destroyed, and marked by discovered bones.

l: land northward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The land northward, called Desolation, lies beyond a small neck separating it from the land southward. The Nephites guard it against Lamanite overrunning. It has large bodies of water, receives migrants from Zarahemla, is approached through a pass, and is supplied by ship.

l: the land southward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_called Bountiful [the land on the southward] The land southward is called Bountiful in the area described. It includes the lands of Nephi and Zarahemla and is nearly surrounded by water.

l: the proclamation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A proclamation sent by the king of the Lamanites throughout his land and surrounding regions. It protects Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their preaching brethren from harm and expulsion, and grants them free access to houses, temples, and sanctuaries so they may preach as they desire.

l: the creation of Adam, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_expounded_in the scriptures [by Aaron to the king] Aaron begins teaching the king from the creation of Adam, explaining how God created man after his own image and gave him commandments.

l: the last day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The last day is a time of resurrection when God raises the faithful. Those who do not repent are cast off, prompting a king to seek salvation, while Alma teaches that those who trust God will be lifted up to glory.

l: the king’s sins, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The king offers to give away all his sins in order to know God and receive salvation. Aaron instructs him to repent of all his sins.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Converted Lamanites took the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies, ceased being called Lamanites, laid down weapons of rebellion, became industrious and free from the curse of God, and became friendly with and established correspondence with the Nephites.

l: city of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a city [chief city of the land of Nephi] The city of Nephi is the chief city in the land of Nephi. Amalickiah enters it with his armies and takes possession of it after the king is assassinated.

l: weapons of rebellion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Converted Lamanites laid down weapons of rebellion and war, ending their fighting against God and their brethren.

l: conversion of the king and his people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lamanite king, his household, and many others were converted through preaching, revelation, prophecy, and miracles; believers gained truth and never fell away.

l: burial of weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The burial of weapons of war is practiced by the Anti-Nephi-Lehies and Lamanites who join them. Converted Lamanites lay down rebellion, stop fighting God and their brethren, and bury swords and other weapons deep in the earth as testimony to God and men that they will never again shed their brethren’s blood, becoming righteous.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (king), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Anti-Nephi-Lehi is king and leader of the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. He commands them not to prepare for war, teaching them to bury their swords because God has forgiven them. Fearing Nephite destruction for murders and sins, he accepts slavery as repayment and will go to the Nephites if commanded by the Lord.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (Lamoni's brother), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Anti-Nephi-Lehi meets with Ammon and his brethren and Lamoni in the land of Ishmael to consider how to defend themselves against the Lamanites.

l: murder, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Murder is a sin committed by the Anti-Nephi-Lehies against the Nephites. After recognizing their many murders, they repent, abhor shedding their brethren’s blood, and accept death rather than murder again; their former acts also sting Lamanites who killed their brethren, leading them to repent.

l: guilt and stains, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: God takes away the guilt from the hearts of the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and removes their stains. Their bright swords become a testimony that they have not stained them again with the blood of their brethren.

l: forgiveness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: God forgives the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi for their many sins and murders through the merits of his Son. This forgiveness leads them to avoid staining their swords again.

l: covenant with God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi covenant with God that they would give up their own lives rather than shed the blood of their brethren. They also covenant to give to a brother rather than take away and to labor abundantly rather than spend their days in idleness.

l: massacre of the Anti-Nephi-Lehies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a massacre [in which a thousand and five were slain without resistance] The Lamanites slay 1,005 people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi while those people call on the name of the Lord and offer no resistance. The massacre causes many of the Lamanites to feel sorrow, repent, and abandon their weapons.

l: more than a thousand converts, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: More than a thousand Lamanite converts, actual descendants of Laman and Lemuel, come to a knowledge of the truth and join the people of God. Brought into God’s fold, light, and salvation, they rejoice, bury their weapons from love for brethren, hate sin, and choose martyrdom rather than kill an enemy.

l: enlightenment and apostasy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: makes state worse than ignorance [when people fall into sin after knowing righteousness] The unit teaches that people who have been enlightened by the Spirit of God and gained knowledge concerning righteousness, then fall into sin and transgression, become more hardened than if they had never known those things.

l: peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Peace is received by people in the kingdom of God at the last day and exists continually among the Nephites. Believing Lamanites bury weapons and suffer rather than sin. Humility after preaching brings four years of peace, while later conflict ends when Morianton’s people covenant to keep peace.

l: seed of Amulon and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The seed of Amulon and his brethren, priests of Noah, is nearly slain by Nephites; its remnant persecutes believing Lamanites, then is hunted, scattered, and slain.

l: east wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_north_of land of Nephi [in relation to the Lamanites’ possessions] The east wilderness is cleared of Lamanites and settled by inhabitants from the land of Zarahemla and surrounding areas. Moroni places armies and fortifications there.

l: battles, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Lamanites have many battles with the Nephites and are driven and slain. When the Lamanites cannot overpower the Nephites, they return again to their own land.

l: death by fire, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Death by fire is suffered by Abinadi and believers; many Lamanite believers die, fulfilling Abinadi’s prophecy.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The law of Moses is observed and taught by Nephites and converted Lamanites because it is not yet fulfilled. Its ordinances are kept strictly, not as the source of salvation, but to strengthen faith in Christ until he is revealed and fulfilled.

l: words of Abinadi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The words of Abinadi concerning the seed of the priests who caused him to suffer death by fire are brought to pass when their seed are hunted, scattered, and slain.

l: gospel of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The gospel of God is associated with the power of God's word that brought the Lamanites to repentance and caused them to sing redeeming love. Through it, people could learn the mysteries of God and receive salvation.

l: love, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Love for brethren motivates Lamanites to bury weapons, bridle passions, and accept death rather than kill enemies.

l: joy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Joy is felt by the speaker through God-given success: the conversion and repentance of many Lamanites, the success of his brethren, and being an instrument in God’s hands. It becomes full, leads him to boast, praise, and thank God, and grows until his soul is carried away as it were from the body.

l: instruments in God's hands, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: bring_about conversion of the Lamanites [as servants of God] Ammon and his brethren were instruments in God's hands in bringing the Lamanites into God's light and fold. They attribute the great and marvelous work to God rather than to their own strength or wisdom.

l: chief judge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: issues proclamation [throughout all the land concerning admitting the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi] The chief judge received Alma and his brethren and heard what had happened among the Lamanites. He sent a proclamation throughout the land seeking the people’s voice concerning admitting the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The land of Jershon, east by the sea and joined to land Bountiful, was given by the Nephites to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi for an inheritance. It became a place where the people of Ammon and a church were established after the Lamanites were driven out. It received Alma, Amulek, their brethren, and cast-out Zoramites. Later it served as a gathering and guarded place for Nephite armies as Moroni met the Lamanites.

l: land Bountiful, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Land Bountiful is a Nephite-protected land, bordered by Teancum’s and Amalickiah’s camps. Moroni fears its loss could threaten Nephite liberty; Teancum repulses approaching Lamanites at its borders. Moroni then fortifies it and secures the narrow pass, while Lehi protects the city. Lamanite prisoners build a ditch and high timber-and-earth wall around the city, making the land an exceeding stronghold where they are guarded.

l: people of Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The people of Ammon, formerly called the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and formerly Lamanites, were numbered among the church of God. They were marked by zeal toward God and men, perfect honesty, uprightness, and firm faith in Christ. Established in Jershon, they abhorred shedding their brethren’s blood, refused weapons, and would suffer death rather than fight, trusting in Christ and the resurrection. They received the poor Zoramite believers, providing food, clothing, lands, and care according to need. In Jershon they also took Korihor, bound him, and brought him before Ammon, who had him carried from the land. They eventually left Jershon for Melek so Nephite armies could use the land.

l: war against the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: War against the Nephites is a conflict between Nephites and Lamanites, driven by anger toward Nephite religion and waged against their religion, liberty, lands, and country. Lamanites fear the fighting and many resist gathering. Amalickiah prepares a large army and leads it. Moroni demands surrender; later Moroni and Lehi defeat Jacob’s Lamanites, with heavy deaths, Moroni wounded, Jacob killed, and survivors surrendering or captured.

l: destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a work [among the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi] The Amalekites and Lamanites brought destruction upon the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. Ammon and his brethren were moved with compassion when they saw this destruction.

l: bondage, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Bondage is ended for the fathers by divine deliverance, then threatened by Amalickiah; Moroni and covenanting young men defend Nephite freedom from slavery.

l: inheritance lands in Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a inheritance [for the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi] The Nephites gave the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi the land of Jershon for an inheritance. The people went down into the land and took possession of it.

l: armies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Armies protect the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi in Jershon from enemies, placed between Jershon and Nephi and maintained by a portion of the people’s substance.

l: conversion of Alma, Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a conversion Alma related his conversion, together with the conversion of Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. His account caused great joy among them.

l: victory of Christ over death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a victory [over death] The people of Ammon believed that Christ’s victory over death swallowed up death for them. This belief helped them refuse to fight against their brethren even when facing death.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The armies of the Nephites, composed of Nephites and commanded by Moroni, defend the lands of Jershon and Zarahemla. Equipped with protective armor, thick clothing, shields, swords, cimeters, and other weapons, they fight, drive, scatter, defeat, pursue, and surround Lamanite forces. Moroni’s army grows through liberated Nephite prisoners, refugees from Nephihah, additional men under the standard of liberty, and union with Pahoran’s forces. It captures city Gid after surrounding its Lamanite forces, captures Nephihah by lowering men over its wall, and ultimately pursues and defeats the Lamanites.

l: battle, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A tremendous battle between the Nephites and Lamanites brings tremendous slaughter, unprecedented among the people in the land since Lehi left Jerusalem. The Nephites gain power and defeat the Lamanites; fighting resumes after Zerahemnah refuses an oath and ends when he promises peace.

l: mourning and lamentation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_heard_throughout land [among all the people of Nephi] Mourning and lamentation were heard throughout the land among the people of Nephi. Widows, fathers, daughters, and brothers mourned for kindred who had been slain.

l: destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: causes many thousand lives [from the first year to the fifteenth] The wars brought about the destruction of many thousands of lives and an awful scene of bloodshed.

l: bloodshed, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a awful scene [from the first year to the fifteenth] The period from the first year to the fifteenth year of the reign of the judges brought about extensive bloodshed, with many thousands slain.

l: never-ending happiness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a state [at the right hand of God] It is received according to desires of happiness and good. Wickedness never was happiness.

l: inequality of man, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The loss of kindred reveals man’s inequality, arising from sin, transgression, and the devil’s power.

l: sorrow, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Sorrow arises from death, destruction, and lost kindred among men, unfolding through solemn sorrowful days, fasting, and prayer.

l: rejoicing, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_because_of light of Christ [unto life] Some mourners rejoice and exult because they have hope and knowledge, according to the promises of the Lord, that their kindred are raised to dwell at the right hand of God in never-ending happiness.

l: light of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: leads_to life The light of Christ brings life and is identified as the reason for joy amid death and destruction.

l: this people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The speaker has been called to preach the word unto this people and has received much success in doing so.

l: the fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The fathers are held in captivity, then delivered from bondage by the Lord; God establishes a church among them.

l: evil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Evil comes before all people and is distinguishable to those who know it. Those ignorant of good and evil are blameless; those who know both receive according to desire. It should be resisted with words, or swords against rebellion when necessary.

l: captivity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Captivity is the fathers’ condition of bondage, remembered by the speaker and Alma as a state from which the Lord and God delivered them repeatedly.

l: holy calling, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_given_to the speaker [to preach the word] The Lord called the speaker by a holy calling to preach the word unto this people.

l: success, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_given_to the speaker [by God] The speaker has received much success in preaching, and he rejoices even more in the success of his brethren who went to the land of Nephi.

l: the fruit of their labors, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_brought_forth_by brethren [in abundance] The fruit of the brethren’s labors consists of those who may enter the kingdom of God and praise Him forever.

l: the merciful arm, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_extended_towards the speaker [by the Lord] The speaker remembers the Lord’s merciful arm, which the Lord extended toward him.

l: Anti-Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Korihor, a man called an Anti-Christ, came into the land preaching against prophecies of Christ’s coming.

l: Korihor, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Korihor, an Anti-Christ, teaches that there is no God, Christ, or atonement and leads many into wickedness. After demanding a sign from Alma, he is struck dumb, admits the devil deceived him, begs for food after being cast out, and dies among the Zoramites.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Ammon, a high priest and Alma’s fellow laborer, joins Alma and others preaching among the Zoramites, receiving Alma’s prayer for strength.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The Zoramites are a people separated from the Nephites and led by Zoram, living in Antionum. They build synagogues and worship weekly at the holy stand, but their worship is marked by prayers meant to be heard and praised by people. They deny Christ’s coming, believe salvation is for themselves as a chosen people, and are characterized by pride, riches, fine goods, and great errors that pervert the ways of the Lord. After the word destroys their craft, they become angry, exile believers in the preached words, and refuse to hearken. A son’s conduct further damages their willingness to believe. They stir up the Lamanites against the people of Ammon and the Nephites, prepare for war, then become Lamanites and join their armies, with their leaders serving as chief captains and inspiring fierce fighting.

l: prophecies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: are_spoken_by prophets [concerning the coming of Christ] The prophecies concerned the coming of Christ and were described by Korihor as foolish traditions. Alma defended them and testified that Christ would come.

l: sign, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: After Korihor demands a sign, Alma declares God will give one: Korihor is struck dumb.

l: curse, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_not_taken_off Korihor Korihor recognized that his dumbness was a curse brought upon him after he withstood the truth. Alma refused to ask that the curse be taken away because Korihor would again lead away the hearts of the people.

l: Korihor's dumbness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Korihor's dumbness, a curse by God's power, began after Alma's declaration and persisted through his casting out.

l: Korihor's death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_caused_by Zoramites [he was run upon and trodden down] Korihor was run upon and trodden down among the Zoramites until he was dead. His death was presented as the end of one who perverted the ways of the Lord.

l: law against belief, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Law against belief is forbidden by God: it would violate God’s commands and create unequal grounds; punishment applies to crimes, not belief.

l: crimes, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The son's crimes are judged by law, cannot be hidden from God, and testify against him at the last day unless he repents.

l: Antionum, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Antionum is the land of the Zoramites, east of Zarahemla near the seashore and south of Jershon; Zoramites gather there, then Lamanite armies gather before moving toward Manti.

l: Helaman, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Helaman is a son of Alma, brother of Moroni, keeper of sacred records, preacher, church leader, and military leader. In his youth, Alma teaches him to remember the captivity of their fathers, trust God, keep God’s commandments, and counsel with the Lord. Alma entrusts him with sacred records, plates, interpreters, and the duty to preserve a record of the people, while warning that transgression would lead to being delivered to Satan. Helaman believes in Jesus Christ, promises to keep Alma’s commandments, declares God’s word, and reestablishes the church throughout the land with his brethren. He persuades the people of Ammon to keep their oath not to take up weapons, then leads their two thousand young men, later two thousand and sixty, in defense of the Nephites. He directs campaigns and stratagems against the Lamanites, commands Nephite forces, records victories and losses, and attributes the preservation of the young men to their faith and God’s miraculous power. He gains lost lands with exceeding success but endures hunger, thirst, fatigue, and other afflictions while awaiting support. After receiving six thousand men and provisions, he preserves his part of the land, returns to preaching, and helps establish the church again. He receives sacred things from Shiblon, sends engravings throughout the land except restricted parts, and dies at the end of the thirty-fifth year.

l: Corianton, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: goes_to land northward [in a ship to carry provisions] Corianton had gone forth to the land northward in a ship to carry provisions to the people who had gone there.

l: Rameumptom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Rameumptom is the Zoramites’ holy high stand at synagogue centers, where one person at a time stands to offer prayer and worship.

l: synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Synagogues are places for worship of God, built by the poor in heart and used by Zoramites on the day of the Lord. They contain a raised Rameumptom for standing and praying, yet poor people are cast out because of apparel and poverty.

l: separation of the Zoramites from the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The separation of the Zoramites from the Nephites caused Alma great sorrow. The Nephites feared that this separation would lead the Zoramites to correspond with the Lamanites.

l: worship at the holy stand, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Worship at the holy stand is a Zoramite practice requiring a repeated public prayer, followed by silence about God until the next gathering. Alma counters the belief that exclusion from synagogues prevents worship, teaching worship and scripture study elsewhere; Nephites seek to preserve worship according to their desires.

l: Alma's prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma's prayer asks God for strength amid the Zoramites' wickedness, comfort in Christ, and success, power, and wisdom for him and his fellow laborers to bring the Zoramites again unto God; afterward, his companions receive strengthening.

l: poor class of people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A group of people, poor and cast out of synagogues for their apparel and poverty, is esteemed as dross until preachers begin to have success among them after much labor.

l: the poor in heart, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Poor in heart are impoverished people despised and cast out of synagogues; affliction humbles them, bringing them to Alma and preparing them to hear God’s word.

l: Onidah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_a place [where the Lamanites fled and gathered] Onidah is the place where the Lamanites who refuse to fight the Nephites flee. They gather there at the place of arms and appoint a king and leader over themselves.

l: worship of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Worship of God extends beyond synagogues and weekly observance, teaching cast-out poor people that they can worship despite exclusion.

l: poverty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: causes humility [when people are despised and cast out because of it] Poverty causes the people to be despised by their brethren and priests and to be cast out of the synagogues. Their poverty brings some of them to a lowliness of heart.

l: affliction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: causes humility [among the poor in heart] The afflictions of the poor have truly humbled them and placed them in a preparation to hear the word.

l: knowledge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: is_perfect in that thing [when the word has swelled the soul and enlightened understanding] Knowledge is distinguished from faith because a person who knows a thing has no cause to believe it. Knowledge becomes perfect in a particular matter when the word has enlarged the soul and enlightened the understanding, though faith is not thereby to be laid aside.

l: experiment upon the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
