s: consists_of planting the seed [to test whether the seed is good] An experiment upon the word begins when a person awakens and exercises even a particle of faith or a desire to believe. The person gives place for the word, observes whether it swells and grows, and learns whether the seed is good.

l: seed (Alma's listeners' seed), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma's listeners' seed is the word planted in the heart. Accepted without unbelief, it swells, sprouts, grows, enlarges the soul, enlightens understanding, and strengthens faith. Nourished by faith, it becomes a tree leading to everlasting life; neglected or resisted, it does not grow.

l: tree (the planted word), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: A seed sprouts into a tree. It needs great care, nourishment, faith, diligence, and patience; otherwise, without root and scorched, it withers away. Nourished, it brings forth fruit and, as the planted word in Alma's listeners, springs up unto everlasting life.

l: fruit, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The fruit of the tree comes from nourishing the tree with faith, diligence, patience, and long-suffering. Most precious, sweet, white, and pure above all, it satisfies hunger and thirst when feasted upon.

l: everlasting life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Everlasting life results as the planted word takes root and becomes a tree, nourished through faith, diligence, and patience until it springs up.

l: being cast out of the synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Being cast out of the synagogues leaves the poor without a place to worship God and causes them to be despised because of their poverty. Their exclusion can bring them to humility and prepare them to hear the word.

l: Zenos, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Zenos, an old prophet, testifies that God mercifully hears prayer and turns away judgments because of his Son.

l: Alma's listeners, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Alma's listeners, cast out of synagogues, ask whether to believe in one God and how to begin faith by planting the word in their hearts.

l: enemies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: The enemies spread death, murder the people, and gain possession of lands when the people are weakened by neglect and internal conflict.

l: the judgments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: come_upon the people [because of slothfulness and neglect] Moroni fears that the judgments of God will come upon the people because of the government's slothfulness and neglect. He says the righteous may be slain while judgment comes upon the wicked.

l: type raised in the wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: provides healing [to those who look upon it] A type was raised in the wilderness so that whoever looked upon it might live. Many looked and lived, while those who would not look because they did not believe perished.

l: healing, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: comes_through type raised in the wilderness [by looking upon it in belief] Healing is presented as possible by looking upon the type raised in the wilderness. Alma asks whether people would look quickly if they could be healed merely by casting about their eyes.

l: mankind, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: Mankind is a fallen group: through the fall it is carnal, sensual, devilish, cut off from the presence of the Lord, and subject to justice. Without the atonement it is hardened, lost, and must perish. This life is a probationary preparation to meet God, perform labors, repent, and choose good or evil. After departing the mortal body, its spirits are taken home to God and retain soul between death and resurrection. At an appointed, unknown time, mankind rises from death and is judged according to works, the desires of the heart, law, and justice. What it sends out is restored: good and desires of happiness bring restoration unto good and happiness; evil brings restoration unto evil. Mercy, justice, and righteous judgment are likewise received according to conduct. Those who repent and desire righteousness to the end are rewarded unto righteousness, redeemed of the Lord, and taken from endless night of darkness. Mankind is ultimately its own judge through its choices.

l: sacrifice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: fulfills law of Moses [great and last sacrifice] There must be a great and last sacrifice that is not a sacrifice of man, beast, or fowl. This sacrifice is the Son of God, and it fulfills the law of Moses.

l: war preparations, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma
s: War preparations were defensive measures during war between the Lamanites and Nephites in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges. They centered on walls, fortifications, earthworks, timber structures, pickets, towers, and secure places. Moroni and Teancum strengthened cities, land Bountiful, and its narrow pass, while Moroni supplied armies and relieved women and children from famine and affliction.
